kafile_uyeleri.tanim: An eleven-year-old elder sister clutching her younger siblings' hands tightly beneath a torn felt shawl.
A nine-year-old boy wearing his father's scorched quiver slung over his neck, his knees scraped raw by mountain stones.
The youngest orphan of seven winters, pressing a rag doll to her chest, her voice hoarse from the biting frost.

giris.satir: M-master guard, do not lower your spear upon us... We are no brigands. We fled Karacaviran village in the lower valley; when horsemen torched the crops, our mother hid us inside the stone culvert of the millrace. For three days we climbed this mountain trail watching the smoke.

secenekler.metin: Tremble not, children, draw near the torchlight. Did none of your elders survive, or does anyone follow behind you?
What is that scorched quiver around your neck and the bundle on your back; did you encounter outlaws on the road?
If we admit you in this dead of winter, whose hearth will shelter you; can your hands perform any labor?

konu_savas_kacisi.satir: We have no one left, uncle guard... Our father fell holding the mill weir, and our mother sent us up the back ravine saying, 'The hearth of the gatekeeper still smokes; go cling to his hem.' Little Bala's feet are nearly frozen; grant us but a handful of warm ash.

secenekler.metin: Children are not put to heavy labor in our village; until you come of age, you shall be entrusted to a household or our own hearth.
Your words are heard; wait before the gate while I render my decision.

konu_emanet_heybe.satir: In the bundle are only two dry barley flatbreads wrapped by our mother and our father's broken whetstone, master. Sungurcuk refused to leave our father's empty quiver behind; he carries it saying, 'When I grow into a youth on the twenty-eighth day, I shall apprentice to Karaca Usta and defend the village.'

secenekler.metin: Which way did the horsemen who struck your village ride; did none of your elders remain?
Your bundle is clean; step aside and wait.

konu_hane_emaneti.satir: We cannot lift heavy quarry stones or drive the plow, master; we are too young. Yet we covet no one's bread. Whatever household or mother you entrust us to, we shall sit dutifully by their hearth; and when we grow into youths, we shall serve as apprentices to the masters and repay our debt.

secenekler.metin: Enter, my little ones; I entrust you to a village household and my wife's hearth.
Our granary is strained and no beds remain; seek another encampment.

kabul_sonuc.satir: May Heaven never let your hearth go cold, uncle guard! Color returns to Bala's cheeks already; the day we come of age, we shall be the most faithful apprentices of this village.

ret_sonuc.satir: Elif gathers her younger siblings beneath her shawl; without a word, the children turn back toward the dark mountain footpath.

veda.satir: With our breath and prayers united, we await your judgment, uncle guard.
